div.head: V Atr 27
div.ab: ⁊ ymbe scipfyrðunga, swa man geornost mæge, þæt æghwylc geset sy sona ofer eastran æghwylce geare.
⁊ ymbe scipfyrðunga, swa man geornost mæge, (gif man þæt geræde) þæt æghwylc geset sy sona ofer eastran æghwylce geare.
⁊ ymbe scipfirðrunga, swa man geornost mæge, þæt æghwilc geset sy sona ofer eastron æghwilce geare.
⁊ ymbe scipfirðrunga, swa man geornost mæge, þæt æghwilc geset sy sona ofer eastron æghwilce geare.
and ymbe scipfyrðrunga, swa man geornost mæge, þæt æghwylc geset sy sona ofer Eastran æghwylce geare.
Und um Schiffszurüstung, wie man eifrigst vermag (wenn dies verordnet wird G2), dass jedes [Schiff] hergerichtet sei bald nach Ostern in jedem Jahre.
And for the equipping of ships, as eagerly as possible (if that is ordered, G2), so that each [ship] is fitted out soon after Easter every year.
And the fitting out of ships as diligently as possible, so that in every year they may all be equipped soon after Easter.
and about the supplying of ships, as zealously us possible, so that each may be equipped immediately after Easter every year.
and the provisioning of ships as fully as possible so that they will be prepared just after Easter each year.
div.note: G2's ‘gif man þæt geræde’ was written above the line in the 12th century.
mæge: G2 adds gif man þæt geræde in Wulfstan’s handwriting

Ein fyrðung bietet Toller nicht, aber 834 scipfyrðung aus II Cn 10 B, welche Hs. aber ursprünglich -forðung las. Da alle Hss. zuerst -ð- hatten, las Archetyp nicht eine Ableitung von fyrd, auf die die Schreiber vielleicht aus 26, 1 verfielen.—Vgl. Gl Schiff 3d; o. Einl. 4 D

Toller gives no fyrðung, but on 834 scipfyrðung from II Cn 10 B, though that MS originally read -forðung. Since all MSS at first had -ð-, the archetype did not read a derivative of fyrd, which the scribes perhaps hit upon from 26, 1.—Cf. Gl Schiff 3d; above Introduction 4 D
Übernommen in VI Atr 32, 3
Taken over in VI Atr 32, 3

fyrdscipe gearwige erklärt VI Atr. ‘Jeder bereit’ Schmid; ‘every one be stationed’ (postiert) Price-Thorpe: diese Bedd. sind nicht belegt; da settan ‘anordnen, instandsetzen’ von Sachen heissen kann, scheint mir ‘Schiff’ zu ergänzen

VI Atr. explains it as fyrdscipe gearwige. ‘Everyone ready’ Schmid; ‘every one be stationed’ (posted) Price-Thorpe: these meanings are not attested; since settan can mean ‘arrange, put in order’ of things, it seems to me that ‘ship’ should be supplied
Im Winter wagte der Wiking auf kleinem Schiffe keine Heerfahrt; Nicolas Hist. of navy I 20
In winter the Viking did not venture on a campaign in a small ship; Nicolas Hist. of navy I 20
Cf. Sax. Chr. ann. 1008 E, an annal which unfortunately is very obscure.

sona here may perhaps have the meaning ‘immediately’ (see BT. p. 895 s.v.), as otherwise the regulation is extremely indefinite. The Viking raids generally began about that time and continued throughout the summer and autumn.
